blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the gate anchor the repeat-fix window on the change's own commit time (pass `at=` of HEAD's commit timestamp) so it matches the backtest and does not drift with wall-clock review time.
evidence: bugfix_size_gate.py:281 `return repeat_fix_escalates(paths, repo_root=repo_root, base_ref="HEAD~1")` — no `at=` passed, so `repeat_fix_escalates` defaults `until = time.time()`
repeat_fix.py:129 `until = time.time() if at is None else float(at)`
backtest_bugfix_size.py:_measure passes `at=_commit_time(sha)` while the gate does not, so the two anchor the 7-day window differently
backtest docstring/commit claim: 'importing the shipped predicate so the measurement cannot drift from the gate' — but the `at` argument is supplied only on the backtest side
blocking.finding: The shipped gate evaluates the repeat-fix window with `at=None` (wall-clock `now`), but the backtest that is supposed to be identical to the gate passes `at=_commit_time(sha)`. The window anchor therefore differs: the gate uses [now-7d, now] while priors are walked from HEAD~1, so a change reviewed later than its commit time (queued/re-reviewed) sees a window that has drifted forward relative to the change position, and the backtest's recall numbers can diverge from the gate's live behavior despite the diff's stated goal that 'the measurement cannot drift from the gate'.
scenarios: A Gerrit change is pushed, sits in review for several days, then re-reviewed: the gate's [now-7d,now] window no longer matches the window in effect at the change's commit time
Backtest recall/escalation figures used to justify the signal do not match what the gate produces live
